rationale: The red/spike validated this exact rule (8/8 cases green) as a small one-file change with mechanics untouched. Option B (require no-file at intake) was explicitly declined by the user (option A chosen). Option C blunts the gate and misses the real gap (classification, not mechanics).

preMortem.trigger: repro-evidence-binding-gate.ts importing review-assurance-floor.ts creates an import cycle.
preMortem.consequence: tsc build fails or runtime import error.
preMortem.mitigation: Check the import graph before committing; if a cycle exists, extract a tiny shared material-path helper (the classify rule) into a leaf module both import, rather than coupling the two gate files.

preMortem.scenario: The change weakens the gate for genuinely dangerous no-file bugs.
preMortem.trigger: A high-impact bug filed with no file declarations is now intake-exempt.
preMortem.consequence: A risky task skips repro evidence at story_create.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep the high/critical + code-verifiable-risk safety net (still requires it), and rely on the DEV-phase repro-evidence-binding gate to re-check once material files are declared (conservative at intake, firmer at DEV).

preMortem.trigger: A logic error makes the refined rule return not-required for a material-code bug/feature.
preMortem.consequence: The gate stops firing where it should.
preMortem.mitigation: The red/spike regression asserts BOTH directions: docs/refactor/chore/no-file -> not required AND material bug/feature + high-risk-no-file -> required; the smoke fails if either flips.

preMortem.scenario: A consuming smoke pins the old classification and breaks.
preMortem.trigger: repro-evidence-binding-dev-gate-smoke.ts / repro-first-candidate-smoke.ts assert the old required=true for a now-exempt case.
preMortem.mitigation: Update those smokes to the refined behavior in the same change and add the red/spike regression; run npm test green before REVIEW.
